source: Google Sheet: Forged and Sent Workout Library (1M-DqwYO3NNPdksY3rubN-PBkoHeWw2BqDoLpQzjgX7c)
restDayRule: Place templateDay 7 on the user's chosen weekday and count forward, so templateDay 1 is the day after the rest day. Plan day 1 starts on the first date that is the day after the rest day. Optional (templateDay 6) is shown only when the user turns on the 4th training day.
notes: day = plan day 1-365. templateDay = ((day-1) mod 7)+1. Day 365 is templateDay 1 of week 53. exercises are [generic movement, prescription]; resolve the movement through movements.json byEquipment[setup]. theme details (warmup, finisher, notes) are in workout-themes.json keyed 'Program|templateDay'.
sessionDesign: Core days (templateDay 1, 3, 5) are full-body sessions in Forged and Built, and full-body power sessions in Warrior (days 1 and 3). Engine and Warrior day 5 stay conditioning circuits. Optional day 6 is a lighter full-body or conditioning session. Strength and power days end with an arm superset (see armSupersetDesign). Every training day is built to take 45 minutes or less including the warm-up and cool-down (see timeDesign). Training days have no dedicated core block: core is trained on the two recovery days, and loaded carries remain only as auxiliary grip and trunk work.
movementsNote: movements.json is the full exercise library for custom plans. Some movements are not used in any scheduled day and exist only as custom-plan options. Each has a 'video' object {url, channel, views}, except Rest Day.
warmupDesign: Each Core and Optional day has a 'warmup' list of [movement, prescription] pairs: cardio primer, mobility, activation, and a bodyweight primer matched to the day's main pattern. No warm-up movement needs a barbell or dumbbells. Pairs resolve through movements.json like exercises. Recovery and Rest days have an empty list and use the theme warmup text. For Core/Optional days the theme 'warmup' text is only a generic fallback line.
alternatesDesign: alternates.json maps movement -> reason -> up to 4 swap movements (nearest first). Reasons: No Barbell, No Bench, No Pull-Up Bar, No Cable or Machine, Knee, Hip, Low Back, Shoulder, Elbow or Wrist, Low Impact, Any Discomfort. Every alternate is a movements.json entry; resolve the display name through byEquipment for the user's setup. Not medical advice. Injury swaps (Knee, Hip, Low Back, Shoulder, Elbow or Wrist) are built from a joint-by-joint map of every movement: if a movement loads an area, it has an alternate for that area. Alternates are chosen from the same movement family, avoid loading the selected area, and match the rep style (loaded lifts swap to loaded lifts, timed holds to timed holds, jumps to power or low-impact work). Elbow and wrist swaps reduce stress rather than remove it, because nearly every lift grips or presses, so those are marked as reduced-stress options in the notes. Every single injury area has an alternate for every movement that loads it, and the app skips an alternate that loads another selected area. Warm-up and mobility movements are mapped too, but the app does not swap warm-ups yet.
recoveryDesign: Recovery days (templateDay 2 and 4) need no equipment in every setup and are built to take 30 minutes or less: an easy walk (12 minutes; 16 minutes on Engine day 2; a short bear crawl lead on Warrior day 2), two equipment-free core holds from a rotating pool (2 x 20 to 35 sec), three gentle mobility moves (2 rounds of 30 sec holds) and a 3-minute breathing finisher. Their movements resolve to the same equipment-free exercise in all four setups. Core work for the whole plan lives on these days.
coachingDesign: Day-level warm-up, finisher and coaching notes are written for a first-time gym goer in a personal trainer voice (purpose, RPE and RIR explained, rest times, progression, deload, soreness, scaling). Each movement also has a long-form howTo (Setup, Move, Watch for, Tip) next to its short cue. General coaching, not medical advice. Each day also has a separate purpose field explaining what the day is for.
armSupersetDesign: The strength and power days end with a two-exercise arm superset (biceps curl A1, triceps A2): Forged and Built days 1, 3, 5 and 6, and Warrior days 1 and 3. Forged and Built use 3 rounds (week 4 deload 2) and Warrior uses 2 rounds (week 4 deload 1). Engine has no arm superset because its circuits already train the arms, and recovery, rest, interval, metabolic and combat days have none either. It adds about 4 to 6 minutes and is included in the 45-minute budget. The day object carries a superset field with the indices of the two exercises in the exercises list. Pairings rotate by template day and by 4-week block.
timeDesign: Training days (templateDay 1, 3, 5, 6) are budgeted at 45 minutes or less including a 7-minute warm-up and a 4-minute cool-down. The 'minutes' value on each day is the planned maximum over all 52 weeks rounded up to 5, so lighter conditioning and combat days show 35 or 40. Recovery days are 30 minutes or less ('minutes' 30; 20 on Warrior day 2). Model: about 35 sec per working set, 30 sec between exercises, rest exactly as written in each prescription, circuits at the listed work and rest, arm superset about 2 x 35 sec plus 50 sec rest per round. Set counts are capped at 3 per exercise (power sets at 3) and peak week 3 raises intensity (RPE, RIR, rest) instead of adding sets. Circuit work-to-rest ratios progress by block while each station keeps a constant cycle time. Round counts are  4, 5, 6 and 3 (deload) for Engine circuits.
